items.full_text: I think this course is truly amazing: the structure, the instructors, the 4Geeks culture... It's an exceptionally comprehensive program, covering every aspect needed to launch a career in development, from front end to back end (my favorite). I can't believe it's almost over—it flew by so quickly, and I'm a bit sad it's ending, but this is just the beginning of my developer journey! Thanks to Ernesto and Slavina, especially Ernesto for being the ideal mentor to start this adventure. Thank you to all the mentors in my 1-on-1 sessions who kept me going, and to Laura, Daniel, and the admin team for their invaluable support throughout. It was daunting at first (and still is), but having such amazing people guide us made it so much smoother. Can't wait to see what's to come. Additionally, the daily live coding sessions, regular peer feedback, and hands-on projects reinforced each concept and created a collaborative, supportive atmosphere that boosted my confidence and practical skills.

items.full_text: The experience has been challenging so far but I'm just trying to keep faith that I am learning. I have a college degree and have studied many different subjects, but this learning style has been completely difference for me and has been quite an adjustment. In the first few weeks, I have had to evaluate and realistically plan out how I can logistically code every day, try to keep up with the course, and handle everything I need to for my personal life and my current job. Maybe its a little bit of imposter syndrome or I need to go further along in the course before I have confidence in my web development abilities but I have been constantly questioning whether or not I'm properly learning the course material and what I can do to increase my retention. Joao and Chris have been fantastic instructors (I would give them a 10/10). I appreciate that they have gone the extra mile to be available and assist us individually and during class.

items.full_text: For me the experience has been both good and bad. I have learned more while here than I have while trying to teach my self on my own, but I think I could know and understand more with some changes. I think the overall curriculum is "good" but misses out on helping people truly understand all that they need to know. Some classes with teachers are "good", but not all classes leave me feeling like that, and we lose time on explaining the harder concepts and focus a bit too much on doing the exercises only. I think overall there is a good attempt to teach people how to learn how to program, but we are still missing out on some necessary items to make it a great experience.

I think it would be better to find a better approach, I am not advocating we don't do the exercises at all in class, but that should really be the only thing we do. We also need to make sure it is not just one or some people spending a lot of time doing things.

items.full_text:
How was your experience in your mentoring session with Yeju [Julie] Motley?

I was struggling with something very foundational for the course and for my future job, she helped walk me through Github repositories and walked me through a lot of Github stuff. I can’t really sum it up because it was so much, but I can see it in my head like how to navigate things. What I was doing before the mentoring session was causing me a lot of technical weirdness especially with the Postcard project, and it was really slowing me down. Yeju helped me get on the right track and I feel confident in my ability to power through the pre-work and I’m looking forward to future mentoring sessions with her and others. She also gave me lots of tricks on how to be successful in the course.

items.excerpt: I like the teachers very much. They are helpful, knowlegeable and always available. I think the course material needs improvement. The text material is very basic and lacking and it also lacks a more progressive set of exercises. For example, the...
items.full_text: I like the teachers very much. They are helpful, knowlegeable and always available. I think the course material needs improvement. The text material is very basic and lacking and it also lacks a more progressive set of exercises. For example, the lessons are very basic and the exercises in the end of each lesson seems far more advanced than what we have learned, leaving a gap of knowledge between them. Also the course material is all text based and lack real world examples of the technology presented. I always find myself looking for other resources like YouTube to learn the topics. Video lessons would be very useful.

items.excerpt: Shane shows he is very knowledgeable, welcoming personality, and cares about answering our questions. However, the following areas can be improved: pacing of class, use of logical sequence when explaining concepts, balancing he amount of teacher vs...
items.full_text: Shane shows he is very knowledgeable, welcoming personality, and cares about answering our questions. However, the following areas can be improved: pacing of class, use of logical sequence when explaining concepts, balancing he amount of teacher vs student air time, catering to different levels of students, better utilizing TA in class with breakout rooms or other techniques, having data informed instruction, giving opportunity for repetition in order to internalize new skills as opposed to long winded lectures, having certain rules to have class run smoothly (telling students when is an appropriate time or method for asking questions, etc)

items.full_text: I genuinely expect to do more in-person stuff, I did thoroughly ask if there was going to be an in person option, I was assured there would be an online option as well. The online alternative is alright I guess, its just now what I desired. Kind of disappointed in the lack of in person time I've been able to have as I've requested many times to attend in person but the TA won't attend as not enough in-person people attended. I wish I would've been more informed about the situation, but I am at fault for not asking enough questions. I do see my self dedicating more time and I feel I'm learning even if its online. It's just I extremely DESPISE almost HATE doing classes online , which is what prevented me from pursuing my career further in the first place because of covid. I hope something can be done while I'm still in this course where more in-person options will be available, as of now I cant see my self recommending this coding BootCamp. Maybe I change my mind by the end.

items.excerpt: Im not sure , I appreciate the enthusiasm and many resources available (breathecode , mentoring even after graduating, and great course with its content) , but I cant get past the complete lack of in person options. Maybe I would recommend it for...

items.full_text: There should be a better system of hiring instructors. They should know the curriculum from day 1 and they should be able to understand what problems novice coders will face when confronted with more difficult concepts and be able to come up with solutions for that. The examples and lectures should be planned, not filled with technical difficulties and awkward pauses. Especially with a rushed syllabus. PERIOD. They should also make a more approachable class, there's a reason that the same 3-4 students are the only ones asking questions.

items.full_text: Mentors are awesome, feels like 35%-45% class feels useful. In breakout rooms when working on projects and getting feedback, most of the time is very useful. Most times when we are getting lectured on a new concept time does not feel useful. Examples are too complex, explanations are long-winded, often ideas are not sequential (first you need to... next...), and little is done to see if we retained information other than vague superficial questions such as: "does that make sense?" or "Any questions?" (sometimes we don't know the questions to ask, maybe we think we know but we don't, etc).

items.excerpt: Shane shows that he cares about us learning, he has a great attitude that makes me feel he wants to be here, I can see that he has experience and knowledge about coding. It is very hard for me to learn material from Shane's teaching style. Apart...
items.full_text: Shane shows that he cares about us learning, he has a great attitude that makes me feel he wants to be here, I can see that he has experience and knowledge about coding. It is very hard for me to learn material from Shane's teaching style. Apart from what I have already commented on, there are times when Shane spends a lot of time troubleshooting something or he speeds through something leaving me feeling lost. I know some things can be out of his control, but I would hope he could be more prepared, or have a "plan b" if something takes more than 3 min to troubleshoot. He certainly has his moments when he can be very helpful and has created a comforting classroom environment, but there has been more negative than positive for me personal time in class.

items.excerpt: The price is great, unlimited mentoring and career services is great, curriculum is decent, staff wants you to succeed and do well, I've had bad experience with live classroom time so that's why I wouldn't say a 10. I think it would be nice if there...
items.full_text: The price is great, unlimited mentoring and career services is great, curriculum is decent, staff wants you to succeed and do well, I've had bad experience with live classroom time so that's why I wouldn't say a 10. I think it would be nice if there were certain standards all teachers are held to and more specific and strategic things in place to address a teacher who may not be lecturing at a high level. Examples could include live in-class observation, more interactive educational platforms (nearpod.com, quizlet, formative.com, etc). It would also be helpful if all teachers at 4geeks taught with data informed instruction. I feel this academy has a lot of potential! but is not producting the best classroom experience

items.full_text: Let's see how the training goes as we go further and deeper into concepts. I think the reading material and exercises are well built and complete and same goes with the projects. I had the opportunity to contact Mattia and Stefany as part of the mentoring program and both have been very helpful, patient and pleasant to deal with! This bootcamp is very important to me and I will dedicate all the time possible so that I can reach a good level of knowledge and hopefully be able to work in the dev field as soon as possible. items.full_text: Summarizing all the elements involved in computer programming is an overwhelming task. The creator of the course does an excellent job holding a student's hand and offering direction. The exercises highlight must-have skills and without them, it is very difficult to understand what exactly to focus on. Considering the varying educational backgrounds of students enrolled, the course dissects the material well while remaining challenging and interesting.

items.excerpt: George is patient, encouraging, empathetic. He pushes students to deliver what they never thought they were capable of before this class. It is so difficult for professional developers to remember what it was like to know absolutely nothing about...
items.full_text: George is patient, encouraging, empathetic. He pushes students to deliver what they never thought they were capable of before this class. It is so difficult for professional developers to remember what it was like to know absolutely nothing about the topic, but George never makes us feel inadequate for lacking knowledge. Nor does he steamroll over us with content that is too advanced for our current level. I am very happy to be in this moment of my journey and I am so excited for my next steps, but I will always remember George fondly as the person I owe a whole new career to.

items.excerpt: We only have 2 days from one class to another to finish the project of the lesson. Although it's not mandatory to finish the project before the next class, in the practice if you haven't done it in time, it gets more difficult to understand and...
items.full_text: We only have 2 days from one class to another to finish the project of the lesson. Although it's not mandatory to finish the project before the next class, in the practice if you haven't done it in time, it gets more difficult to understand and embrace the next lesson (and this problem gets bigger after each lesson and eventually the student feels lost). I would give one more class from one lesson to the next one. And maybe two projects for lesson being mandatory only one, so that if the student has more time he can do 2 projects and embrace better the lesson. But also the students with less time (or that struggles with the lesson) have time to finish their project and be in a better position to understand the next lesson. Unit testing has one lesson but in the next projects it's not mentioned at all. I would include hints to apply unit testing in the project instructions so we can learn to apply it by practice. Same for git commands.

In comparison to the acceptance of other projects in done by other graduates, they assured, that this sometimes was ruther unusal, meaning the degree to which very small discrapencies made the projects get rejected. items.excerpt: Our instructors are very knowledgeable and do their best to challenge us and teach new concepts. But for in-person sessions, I believe going over projects step by step would be more helpful so we can fully understand what and why we’re doing...
items.full_text: Our instructors are very knowledgeable and do their best to challenge us and teach new concepts. But for in-person sessions, I believe going over projects step by step would be more helpful so we can fully understand what and why we’re doing something, and be able to really apply those skills after we graduate. I think that makes more sense, since most people have the same questions and instead of going one by one we can address it as a group and move forward. I also have to use other online courses and resources often to help me understand some concepts instead of just copying and pasting code. Sometimes I find myself being more productive working on the exercises on my own than in class, so maybe less in-person sessions or having the option of online would be much less draining throughout the week

items.excerpt: The course is obviously well thought out in terms of what to approach and when to help with the learning curve. If possible I would revisit some of the pre-work exercises specifically around Javascript to update these and restructure a little. For...
items.full_text: The course is obviously well thought out in terms of what to approach and when to help with the learning curve. If possible I would revisit some of the pre-work exercises specifically around Javascript to update these and restructure a little. For example, there are a number of exercises with filters etc where you learn a number of different approaches but feels messing with the addition of ES6 functions and was a little confusing. Another tweak I could suggest is to add in some additional exercises to reinforce the learnings, often we learn and do the exercise but then we move onto the next section. One example would be the Jest testing section. I have an awareness of this but don't feel confident if I need to take a TDD approach.

items.full_text: THE BEST SO FAR !!!!!! To me is the best Academy Online, after deciding to invest my time/money in this career using 4Geeks as an academy, I've made my own research and competitive analysis across (IronHack, Springboard, NuCamp, Coding Dojo, General Assembly, Lambda School, DevMountain, Etc), and in all aspects, 4Geeks are beyond the competitors, in terms of Syllabus, mentorship, live classes, career support, and more. I continue to support social and professional channels and help to promote the academy every time I could. Just need to mention a suggestion to change how the certificate is designed, for people taking part-time or full-time Bootcamp taking the same syllabus and investing the same effort to learn doesn't make sense and also isn't fair to differentiate certificates, certificates are for the knowledge and differentiate courses by type rest importance and aren't balanced, especially when you need it as a proof.

I said it before, that content on this platform needs to be edited and expanded. Often the example code necessary to complete an assignment was missing from the lesson and I was told to look at the solution. On top of that, I have wasted hours of my time trying to implement code from the lesson materials that was simply incorrect.

items.full_text: The class moves superfast! Everyone at 4Geeks has been very supportive. There were a few times when my GeekMentor 1 on 1 sessions were cancelled in short notice by the mentor, but then I had situations also were I unfortunately had to cancel at the last minute due to my day job holding me over, so I guess things balanced out :) The times when I did have the 1-on-1 sessions were extremely helpful. I appreciate the Geek career virtual field trips, found them very encouraging and makes me feel less fearful of looking for career opportunities. I have found the actual 4Geeks lessons on the website can be confusing and made me feel not very confident about learning, but after adjusting to the idea that w3schools and other online resources are helpful, I feel better about the lessons.

items.full_text: As someone who is learning full-stack and computer science concepts full-time, I find that going to class is not particularly helpful for me, as I learn much more on my own. The instructor is knowledgable but doesn't seem to prepare much beforehand-- it seems he wings it as he goes. I was expecting a more class-like structure, with part of the class time devoted to organized lecture. The tutorials have been helpful, but I find a lot of errors as I go through the course material.

items.full_text: Thank you for creating this survey. My experience of the full-stack program so far is positive, however my initial impression is also disappointing.Those lead me to choose this bootcamp over other bootcamps, such as its syllabus that focuses on pertinent technologies to the market and 4geeks permanent support. I have also important improvable points, like the pre-work was not challenging enough. I have done other pre-works from other bootcamps and with those I have truly struggled and pushed me to learn. I also feel like the classes should be more intense and focused. There is a lot more that can be approached in a 3hour class. It comes uninteresting/frustrating to get to the class, after studying the "Read" Section, and listen to again these introductory concepts as if anew instead of assuming that we are prepared for class and use it to move deeper and practice details of the matter. (Peer connection, support by 4geeks, homework, suggestions for practicing the skills we have lear...

items.excerpt: Carlos is very nice, respectful, patient and cheerful teacher. In several classes I have received his help through some situation I got stuck and I have liked the way he was fluent, and determined not to leave me without solving the issue. Carlos...
items.full_text: Carlos is very nice, respectful, patient and cheerful teacher. In several classes I have received his help through some situation I got stuck and I have liked the way he was fluent, and determined not to leave me without solving the issue. Carlos seems very competent to a student like me, and in several occasions I could absorb his method of thinking from his practical approach. Nevertheless, Carlos must improve his english pronunciation. I know it can very very hard but it is important because it moves the focus from the content of the class to understanding what he is saying and sometimes comes to point of being unintelligible. It would be lovely if Carlos(/4Geeks) gave us projects or tasks, that we could do by ourselves in order to apply the crucial skills we have just learned. It would be for sure optional, but such projects would be much needed in my opinion. It is hard to figure that out alone. E.g. a entire CSS and HTML page, that is within our skillset reach to solidify them..

items.excerpt: Overall, the experience is positive, but in my opinion there are certain aspects that could improve. For me, the biggest reason to enroll in a bootcamp was not to go on a single journey and have exchange with colleagues. I 4geeks bootcamp is very...
items.full_text: Overall, the experience is positive, but in my opinion there are certain aspects that could improve. For me, the biggest reason to enroll in a bootcamp was not to go on a single journey and have exchange with colleagues. I 4geeks bootcamp is very lacking in this aspect as we only work with our colleagues in the final project. We mostly have half an hour session and then are left alone to work on our individual projects. Some of my friends are currently attending other online bootcamp and they all emphasize the sharing aspects of working with buddies in all activities. This way we have the opportunity to share, learn from others, have different insights and also contribute with our strengths.

items.full_text: Right now I understand we are just at the start, so it is hard even to think about recommending it. I am optimistic about it :) It is very hard to answer this survey with the straightness I did because I run the risk of being unfair towards 4 geeks or someone. Hope it won't be the case. Opinions are like asses, everybody has one. I really want to suggest that 4geeks creates a peer dynamics that is inexistent for the moment. There is very little to no interaction between peers because we have no optional challenge, or extra-homework to do. In this way we loose a great opportunity of learning to cooperate or co-code. Schools like 42 are solely based on peer interaction for example. Like I said, it would be optional, and anyone interested could do them alone or message a colleague for cooperation. I think it would be fantastic that there are so many optional projects/tasks advanced by 4geeks/teachers that one would hardly manage to do complete them. Thank you! :)

items.excerpt: The classes are very slow paced. Carlos is a wonderful person and probably very knowledgeable, but he is not stimulating his students. Carlos is merely providing the classes, giving a very strong impression that it is the first time he is reading...
items.full_text: The classes are very slow paced. Carlos is a wonderful person and probably very knowledgeable, but he is not stimulating his students. Carlos is merely providing the classes, giving a very strong impression that it is the first time he is reading the materials at the time he is presenting them in class. This results in frequent mistakes and set up problems. We waist lots of time from the 3hour classes, that if Carlos would be more prepared should be much more condensed with information. He focus on the main picture of the basis and spends lots of time in generalities; he should go on the detail of more advanced things. I feel he is focused on fulfilling only what is expected in the program of 4Geeks and not worried on the development of his students. For this reason we have sometimes one hour of slow unprepared presentation with lots of breaks and the beggining, middle and end. His english skills need to improve as well, it is confusing and unclear communication that demotivates me.

items.full_text: Things being as they are I am not recommending 4Geeks academy unfortunately. The syllabus is very good but the execution is not good enough. I have showed my work at 4geeks to fellow programmers and they started to laugh because what we coded in class was simply wrong. We are not shown real life problems, real life problem solving and even good coding standards/ code reviews / refactoring. This precious class time should not be waisted in the survey. There is no advantage in that, it should be done in another time.

However, having a dedicated mentor from the beginning would have been nice. I understand that people's agendas can change but having someone dedicated from the start would improve the experience. Unfortunately, not everyone has a knack for tutoring either. Maybe having a trial run with the tutor would make the process of deciding on tutors easier.

He was also willing to give extra sessions when needed to explain topics we weren't too confident about. I think he probably has a lot on his plate which is why he can't be our dedicated mentor. If possible, it would have been great for him not only to have been our pre-work mentor but our full-stack mentor as well.

items.full_text: I would definitely get the 4Geeks name out there. The only things that might need improving are the grammar and spelling mistakes in the material. I understand it is bit on the low priority but it might give a more "professional" feel. Also having more of a structure on some of the materials would be better. For instance, there were times in the pre-work that you're busy on a certain topic and then it would state if you don't feel comfortable with that topic just yet try another topic. Wouldn't it be more beneficial to do all of the topics needed first and just give a reference for the student to go back to that topic if they need a refresher.

items.full_text: I know this is a bootcamp, but it's too much. No time to assimilate concepts... I think more practice is needed. Maybe more projects. And maybe classes could be more interactive where students have to resolve certain activities in class. But I understand this depends a lot of the group. Also, the step between React and React with Context and Api, is too small. The jump in between is too short for what it is... something there is missing, is the impression I had. This is way too concentrated and resumed. I understand that doing all of this for the time given, means to do things concentrated but I wouldn't have minded doing a longer training with more time to practice or assimilate. Also, teachers are being great until now, but having two possibilities for mentorships instead of one, would be great.

items.full_text: J.D. is clearly very knowledgeable and pushes us. While his teaching style is not necessarily my preferred style and took a class or two to get use to, I greatly appreciate his drive and his unwillingness to teach to the slowest student. He is willing to give plenty of help and advice, but does not let unprepared students or students who need more help than can be given in a few minutes hold back the class. That said, he does make sure to check in on students he has noticed are struggling to make sure they are reaching out to mentors to get the help they need.

items.full_text: I wouldn't really recommend this school.The program is very complex, almost every lesson we try to do a new project or study a new topic, although the previous topics have not been fully understood.Even if there was one lesson a week, a whole week would be enough to study new material and complete a project, rather than have three lessons a week and at the same time not learn any material and constantly rush to finish all the tasks.Before starting the project, there is not enough basic training on how and what works at the beginning of the course it was and it really helped before starting something global and then it disappeared.Now it’s just complete agony because every time the projects are more and more complex, the topics I don’t understand and at the same time I have to complete everything on time.I'm really thinking about leaving this school because I don't see that I'm learning anything new, besides having to rush through something I don't understand.

items.full_text: As for me, Ernesto is simply a wonderful teacher, for the first time I see a person so patient that he can communicate with students who do not always understand what needs to be done according to the assignment.He always tries to help everyone, no matter how long it takes, and it’s very nice.The only negative is that when I need help and teacher Ernesto always tells me what to write, but I don’t always understand how it works, I just write the code that he tells me. Because of this, it seems like the work has been done, but I still don’t understand this topic.Maybe this takes more time, but that’s why I took the course, to at least understand something, but in the end I just write code that essentially should work, but I don’t understand how it works without the help of a teacher

items.full_text: Amazing teacher and mentors, really great and helpful. The format is not good. Flip classroom, spending most of the lessons working with classmates and learning on my own are not a good method. Other classmates as well agree that when we have long explanations we know what to do during practice, when we have short explanations we feel like we have no idea what to do. We would prefer to have three hours of explanations where we get the tools and then do practice outside of the lessons. Otherwise we spend most of the time just in rooms with classmates where no one knows what we are supposed to do. I feel like I would learn a lot more the other way. At the moment I feel like I am unnecessarily struggling which would be easy to avoid. Mentoring sessions are great and teacher flexible to adapt, which he did and was appreciated. The downside is just the format. Also, I think you should let future students knoe that the course is not for beginner, because it isn't.

items.full_text: I already have recommended it to friends and family of mine, I think its a great way to get into Tech and pursue a career change. Had you asked me three months whether I'd be on track to potentially change my career from Hospitality to Tech, I would've laughed. Firstly the scholarships available to me made it possible to even entertain the idea of changing careers, Secondly the material provided (while not perfect) definitely gave me the foundation to start doing my own research and further my own education. Also, the learnpack program that you've created in GitHub are an absolute asset, I would just suggest to maybe have a crash course in terms of how to properly use GitHub in the beginning of the course or in the Prework in order to really get those concepts down, because I still have issues with it all. I think what it really boils down to is that its A LOT of material, to cover in a very small amount of time, it really separates the people who are serious about this from otherwise

items.full_text: This has been a great way to get started with coding. We've learned to work with Manny and now things are going much smoother because now we're getting better at interpreting all the information. However, I will say, the pace of the course is wild. While its been an altogether good experience, I feel like within the reading and documentation that we have, there's always something missing or maybe its written out of order in terms of building upon previous skills. Like personally, I would implement within the first week of class, to learn about GitHub and all those concepts for two reasons using simple HTML boilerplates. Firstly, it starts exposing the student to reading code and getting used to reading it, and secondly, it gives the professor a chance to set up everyones machine in the same way. As I've come along in the course I was starting to have issues pushing work from my local machine and etc. If this was done in one of our first modules, we'd all have a similar set up to work.

items.excerpt: In the beginning it was difficult, maybe it was the stress of learning a difficult new skill, but as time went on and we started understanding concepts and how to actually read code, Manny's methods begun to make more sense. He's always available to...
items.full_text: In the beginning it was difficult, maybe it was the stress of learning a difficult new skill, but as time went on and we started understanding concepts and how to actually read code, Manny's methods begun to make more sense. He's always available to help, even offering office hours so we can talk to him outside of class time and ask for advice with our projects and lessons. And again, like i mentioned in my previous survey, Manny's really knowledgable, and he's always giving us real world tips in terms of job interviews for the future.

items.excerpt: Andres is the same as before, and always available to help. One thing that he's great at is that whenever class is going and Manny is lecturing, we're able to reach out to Andres via slack and ask him certain questions so we dont interrupt his flow...
items.full_text: Andres is the same as before, and always available to help. One thing that he's great at is that whenever class is going and Manny is lecturing, we're able to reach out to Andres via slack and ask him certain questions so we dont interrupt his flow and take away from the class time (not that Manny doesn't encourage asking questions during class, on the contrary) But with this its a way to be able to get real-time answers while class is going and not take away from the train of thought that might be going on in the demo. And again, extremely knowledgable (he really was in a cohort like we are right now, right before taking on this TA position? like can i get his professor as one of my tutors?)

items.full_text: I would like there to have been more structure on the part of the instructor as well as already created lesson plans and premade visual aids. This would allow us to save time on trying to create while explaining concepts and possibly allow for more interaction with the class as opposed to just explaining topics. In my opinion, It would be more beneficial for the class if there were more real life examples that show the concepts being taught which go over the concepts in real time from start to finish when applicable. I think the instructor is very knowledgable and experienced in the field but I feel he may be struggling to put his thoughts into words at times. On the positive side of things, he is very eager and willing to answer questions and has a very positive attitude towards the class. To be very transparent, I've had to find other sources on the internet to try and learn many of the concepts we have been taught up to this point.

items.excerpt: Manny possesses a wealth of intelligence and patience, qualities that shine especially during our live coding sessions. His spontaneity in deciding to code examples on the spot is admirable, though it sometimes leads to unforeseen challenges...
items.full_text: Manny possesses a wealth of intelligence and patience, qualities that shine especially during our live coding sessions. His spontaneity in deciding to code examples on the spot is admirable, though it sometimes leads to unforeseen challenges mid-way. This approach keeps the sessions dynamic and engaging, albeit occasionally less structured. I've also explored other educational content for comparison, such as Dr. Angela Yu's courses on Udemy. Dr. Yu adopts a highly structured format, comprising an introduction, a problem related to the topic, and a step-by-step solution, followed by a test problem for independent practice. This systematic approach aids in clarity and understanding. While Manny's style differs, often encountering unexpected problems, these moments offer valuable insights into real-world coding challenges. It's a unique learning experience where we witness problem-solving in action, enhancing our understanding of the unpredictability and flexibility required in coding.

His attentiveness and readiness to assist Manny increased our productivity during the coding session. His ability to anticipate and address issues as they arise during these live projects is impressive, contributing significantly to the overall success of the class.

items.excerpt: So this program has been great as a stepping stone to get into the tech industry and becoming a Full-Stack Developer. However, the latter half of the program has been an absolute struggle, where I don't feel comfortable trying to get into the...
items.full_text: So this program has been great as a stepping stone to get into the tech industry and becoming a Full-Stack Developer. However, the latter half of the program has been an absolute struggle, where I don't feel comfortable trying to get into the industry yet, I still feel like theres concepts that I haven't grasped yet. I will say the difficulty of the projet grew exponentially once we got into APIs and using React where I feel like I'm running around trying to find other resources in order to properly know how to code something on my own. Also the lack of demo videos for these complex projects did not help, as I feel like Alejandro Sanchez does a great job of explaining all the concepts.

items.full_text: Emmanuel's a great teacher, I have to say he's always there and available for us to consult with and even goes out of his way to make powerpoint presentations for class, have office hours on days we dont have class to be able to ask questions about projects and move forward with the class. However, perhaps I just don't click with his teaching style as I really don't think I've grasped a lot of concepts that by now if this curriculum were supposed to leave me ready to pursue a career right out of the bootcamp I should have already. This also being his first course teaching, he's just getting into how to teach and perhaps needs to cut his teeth a bit more. Again, not for his lack of trying, and he's very knowledgeable, he's just got learn how to translate some of the concepts to people who have never coded before like myself.

items.excerpt: Having gone through the entire course, I can comfortably say yes I would absolutely recommend 4Geeks to anyone...that lives in Miami and can acquire the scholarship. I do appreciate the fact that I had to go through an interview process to determine...
items.full_text: Having gone through the entire course, I can comfortably say yes I would absolutely recommend 4Geeks to anyone...that lives in Miami and can acquire the scholarship. I do appreciate the fact that I had to go through an interview process to determine whether or not I was in the correct mindset to be invested in to pursue this career. On the other hand I don't know if it was just my cohort, but there we're a couple people that I have NO IDEA how they passed their interview or even got in, like they definitely paid the $10K for the course or had some sort of connection because they don't add anything at all to the class and quite frankly seem even more lost than I am, and I'm not exactly a coding whiz. Also, the course itself is VERY fast, for people that already have a good foundation in coding this course would be great for them. For someone like me on the other hand that had no experience in coding was a huge challenge and wished there was a more indepth course to really grasp concepts

items.full_text: Although we are only 2 weeks the feeling is not at all positive. Starting with the presentation of the first day by the director, I appreciate Director’s motivating message but his English was improvable. I'm not native but if 4Geeks offers such bootcamp in English for Europeans, the director should have a decent level (I know, he apologized several times for his level). As 4Geeks website states "No previous experience needed", but then you see with astonishment how fast the teacher advances and although you may have a thousand doubts in your head, you can hardly put them in order. Of course, there is a Prework module, Slack chats to assist students...However, even if I have previous experience with programming, Github, CLI, I have talked to my peers and they seem to have the same feeling. I'm sure the teacher is a really good professional, but being educator implies other skills. Again, only 2 weeks yet but I personally did 2 months of Full Stack July 2023 and know what I mean

items.full_text: Have done bootcamps before. One was an expensive disaster, and ignored every piece of feedback and plea asking for help to the point of begging, the other was a fraction of the cost and was so good I took 2 courses with them & took to leaving them great reviews without even being asked. Here, there is a lot of Googling the answer and having to work backwards because there is a lot of jumping around screen and the explanations are extremely confusing to the point of frustration. This was sold as a course of ´repetition through learning´ yet I frequently have NO idea how to even approach a problem and I am expected to be self-guiding. I have redone all exercises and find myself extremely uncomfortable each time.

items.excerpt: Edgar tries to explain what he is doing but uses FAR too much tech talk and seems to forget that we have never lived and breath code before. When a problem in an exercise is given, each time, we NEED to read and stop and be ASKED: What do WE think...
items.full_text: Edgar tries to explain what he is doing but uses FAR too much tech talk and seems to forget that we have never lived and breath code before. When a problem in an exercise is given, each time, we NEED to read and stop and be ASKED: What do WE think the issue is? How do WE think we will solve this, string by string, carefully and methodically and wait for student responses (i.e; do we need to set up any variables, define a new function, what existing ones should/can we look for, if I write this, can you tell me what I am missing) otherwise it goes completely over my head and there's too much to even formulate a question for.

items.excerpt: good course planning, prep work and module/lesson structure. However diff to follow concepts in class as is just going through what we already have as opposed to 'learning by explanation or example'. I feel we should be working through another...
items.full_text: good course planning, prep work and module/lesson structure. However diff to follow concepts in class as is just going through what we already have as opposed to 'learning by explanation or example'. I feel we should be working through another project example in the class for more exposure and application of ideas for us to then go and try ourselves. Right now we are just going through answers for the 1 or 2 problems we are given but no opportunity to apply and make enough mistakes. Not sure if the breakout period is too long - teaching/learning/therory should be longer for class time as we can work in pairs in our own time. Also not sure if and when is appropriate to reach out to ask for help.

Shane does an amazing job at explaining everything, I just feel so behind on everything that it feels like I'm constantly trying to catch up. At this point, we're working on Flask and Back-end and I'm still trying to fully get the functionality of Javascript. It really demonstrates that the catalyst of what makes this program successful is having a professor that knows how to teach the material. If I could somehow go back to Javascript to get the foundations solid, everything else would fall into place.

items.full_text: At this point, I can see that 4Geeks has a decent framework to work off of, but it really depends on the professor that you get. After my first couple months in the program, with no idea what to expect I didn't know at what level of understanding I had to be at, and thus now in retrospect I see that we are all extremely lost and looking to other resources like Udemy and freeCodeCamp to make sense of what little information we know. At the point that our cohort was switched which was about 2-3 weeks before our final project, just feels like too little too late, and at best I have a fractured foundation on which to continue my studies and try to piece together and come out successful on the other side. Perhaps with a better method of deciding who teaches, or even hiring from within using former students as teachers who know what we're currently going through, perhaps the program would be more cohesive in its learning style.

items.full_text: I would tell them they need to have LOTS of time to sacrifice and part-time does NO justice to having a commitment to having to practice. The onboarding and being left to your own devices is very uncomfortable. There should be a mandatory date when starting out for a 1-2-1 supervised practice of exercises. I am 2 weeks in and need a LOT of help. Lots of text is thrown at me and I do not have a clue how to interpret it. The examples in the itinerary are not very accessible on beginners and whilst there are resources online, I'm not paying Google for the knowledge or guidance, I am paying 4 Geeks Academy. It has been made clear that Google for example use the ´FizzBuzz´ test in interviews, meaning that people would be expected to turn up, memorise that and deliver from memory. I just got out of a 1-2-1 with a mentor, re-treading ground of the 'Probability' exercise & couldn't even begin it. I didn't know what on Earth to start with, how to perform an idea & didn't get any further!

items.full_text: So far so good, it certainly has been fast-paced (which was to be expected). There is only so much time to fully review the work that we complete and access the mentors/professors, but I feel that the intention is there to help each student along. items.full_text: The material and methodology is really good. I was skeptical at first, but I can attest now that it is working for me (and I am not the most logically inclined person). My main issue is with the teaching method. For now, both of the mentors main concern seems to be to get to the solution to any question as fast as possible. Interest in the learning process of the student and in meeting the student where they currently stand seems to be secondary, if it is a concern at all. Comments like "why did you do X? I did not tell you to do X" or "you were supposed to only copy a part of the solution but copied all of it instead" (with an amused undertone) are not helpful, but clearly do show that there are some gaps in the students understanding. So why not start with some explainations first and making the solution secondary until it is clear that the student has understood?

items.excerpt: Generally, the experience is good. Nikhils demos and explainations are solid and very useful for me once I use them to revise on my own time. Suggestion for improvement: some rhetorical training for better presentation of the material. Less reliance...
items.full_text: Generally, the experience is good. Nikhils demos and explainations are solid and very useful for me once I use them to revise on my own time. Suggestion for improvement: some rhetorical training for better presentation of the material. Less reliance on filler phrases, like the very common "this is a thing". What is this "thing" exactly? Better explainations could be (for the sake of example): - This is another array method to add to your toolbox. - This is a workaround you can use once you get stuck. - This is what we consider the best practice.

items.excerpt: Room for improvement: Empath empathy empathy! And some training in communication skills. The constant light sarcastic understone does nothing to help me feel comfortable with asking questions. Furthermore, when I have a doubt, I don't want that...
items.full_text: Room for improvement: Empath empathy empathy! And some training in communication skills. The constant light sarcastic understone does nothing to help me feel comfortable with asking questions. Furthermore, when I have a doubt, I don't want that doubt to be answered with counterquestions. I am not at the point where I know enough theory to understand my mistake or doubt by myself. I need you to take my by the hand a little bit and to guide me to the solution. Right now, I am much more comfortable looking up the answers to my questions by myself.

items.excerpt: After 6 weeks and the first survey, I can say the experience has improved. I'm not writing a lot in this survey since most of the initial concerns have been shared via email. I still agree to a large extent with the concerns shared, but I have...
items.full_text: After 6 weeks and the first survey, I can say the experience has improved. I'm not writing a lot in this survey since most of the initial concerns have been shared via email. I still agree to a large extent with the concerns shared, but I have managed to move forward and catch up and that helps in the perception of the bootcamp and boosts confidence for what is still to come. However, I think there are many things to improve including, but not limited, to: at least 1 recap class after 3 modules; improve the quality and the way some modules or part of them are organized (sometimes we start a topic by showing a script and outputs without having explained, and then after 2 lessons we see the explanation somewhere); the time spent in class because lately we see Edgar opening the class and after 45 minutes of fast explanation then creating breakout rooms)...

items.excerpt: I think he is making an effort to improve the dynamics of the classes and to enhance the way he teaches. However, I see sometimes he is in a hurry to make the breakout rooms. Once in a breakout you are expecting him to guide you through the exercise...
items.full_text: I think he is making an effort to improve the dynamics of the classes and to enhance the way he teaches. However, I see sometimes he is in a hurry to make the breakout rooms. Once in a breakout you are expecting him to guide you through the exercise but then there is a deathly silence and no one takes the initiative, and suddenly he disappears until the next help request. I know by heart he is a good person with a great background and professional skills, and I'm sure he will get better.

items.full_text: It is nice but I am investing more than 3 hours a day for the course and I still find myself falling behind, I hope we will start repeating things/concepts soon because otherwise I will not be able to submit the projects. For the lessons, they are a little fast and chaotic and the pair programming that happens after is sometimes even more confusing. Mentoring is working well but sometimes we "throw" out hours just for errors caused by the codespaces itself instead of of the code (that is not working because of these e.g. "connection errors", so it makes it more difficult to play with the code in the codespace) and other issues.

items.excerpt: He is very nice and he knows what he is doing, I think the lesson/explanation gets confusing sometimes during the breakout rooms, not because of Edgar - he does his best - but because the solutions/instructions/the exercise is itself sometimes...
items.full_text: He is very nice and he knows what he is doing, I think the lesson/explanation gets confusing sometimes during the breakout rooms, not because of Edgar - he does his best - but because the solutions/instructions/the exercise is itself sometimes imprecise and confusing to us and then he will try to offer us a solution or help us in ways that then we do not always find in the 4geeks documentation. I realise self-research is an important part of the course but having to search continuously takes away so much time and energy, especially when looking at documentation that is not always easy to understand for beginners (and for mentors too sometimes)

items.full_text: Tim is a good mentor, his eagerness to teach and ensure that all students understand the content is noticeable. However, the teaching style (I'm not sure if it's required by the academy, or if it's just Tim's method) is not efficient for me (personally). I feel there is a lack of explanation in some areas. My biggest dissatisfaction lies with the breakout rooms. I would prefer it to be a teamwork effort among the entire class, following the teacher when explaining topics together as a class. The way people learn is different for everyone, and not everyone understands with this dynamic. Tim seems like a very intelligent person and knows what he's doing, but my suggestion is for him to understand each person learning style, because we are all different.

Despite these challenges, I'm enjoying the learning process and staying focused on mastering the skills needed for this field.

items.full_text: I think it is really stupid to say that this is a fullstack dev course when seems that frontend part is focused only in learning a library like Bootstrap which may or may not be used in the future since there are a bunch more out there. Furthermore, in my experience which clients, when they ask for a website (or any other product which, somehow, will represent them), they'll be asking for a certain level of customization that won't be able to be achieved by a prototyped library like Bootstrap. In fact, even the hiring companies may not be using that library so, giving that importance to a single library instead of explaining the real coding languages will be handicap in the development of the students career

items.full_text: Maybe it has to be this way since this bootcamp is really short in duration compared with others, but at this point I feel overwhelmed by how densely packed together the new concepts are in the lessons on the 4Geeks website. It seems like there is a lot of implicit knowledge that is not explicitely talked about, but we are still expected to use. On the other hand I am struggling with the little amount of instruction that is given in the projects. While this "do or die" approach makes you work really hard, I also feel that keeping the success rate reliably high is important both for motivation and progress (especially when you get several projects in a couple of days). One solution could be the addition of fully optional hints that guide you in the right direction.

items.full_text: Now that we're closer to the end, this final part, the back-end is feeling a bit rushed. This is a individual review but I've talked with some other students and it's a sentiment that is generalized. What is it that is missing? Can't really tell because you don't know what you don't know so it's hard to pin point, maybe a bit more context of it all, how things truly fit together in a working environment and not just in learning? Maybe? Also, in more than one occurrence, I feel that whenever we have practice and exercises to assimilate new tools/skills the student experiences a really great and smooth transition but otherwise, when the module is built with the material and straight to a project it's harder to do that same transition. You manage to deliver the project, if you look back on it, now that you have the knowledge fully assimilated you find it to be extremely easy but during production you struggled so much.

items.excerpt: Personally I think he's not the best explaining things. And this is what i have a problem with. I am a spanish native speaker and i chose to do the course in english because that's the language in which programming languages are based. I thought it...
items.full_text: Personally I think he's not the best explaining things. And this is what i have a problem with. I am a spanish native speaker and i chose to do the course in english because that's the language in which programming languages are based. I thought it was going to make it easier for me to understand. But Nikhil's first language isn't english, so some things i get lost in translation. I find myself hearing explanations that sometimes are repetitive and classes most times seem to be him reading what we should have read ourselves. I learn something new every class, but i think i could have been learning much more if someone fluent was teaching it. He knows what he's doing, but he's not good transmitting that. He struggles finding the right words. It makes me regret not having done the course in spanish instead.

items.excerpt: I'd like to suggest the project review should be mandatory even when it's approved. We don't know if we passed because it was good or was it barely enough? Even if it's good I'm sure there's things we could improve upon even if it is not extremely...
items.full_text: I'd like to suggest the project review should be mandatory even when it's approved. We don't know if we passed because it was good or was it barely enough? Even if it's good I'm sure there's things we could improve upon even if it is not extremely necessary at that point in time. I'm the kind of student that I usually do more in the projects than what is asked because I think it's good to explore more things and we're likely to have to learn those things later anyway but it ends up being ignored. It'd be nice to have a more detailed and feedback. If it's a score, general or by some criteria it's up to you of course. It's in our best interest to know from people who actually work in the industry how we're coming along even though we still have so limited knowledge. Since we'll be trying to get a job after this course it's scary to think we're just ok. Just ok is not very competitive in the job market.

items.full_text: I think that there are a lot of good exercises, and the mentors are a really valuable resource. Just again, I think that the level of some students is very low and that makes me think sometimes that I am not going to be able to attain a high level of expertise in software development. I just feel like there should be a minimum level to enter the program. It is too early in the program, so I am sure there is still a lot to learn and hopefully students will catch up. I also need to see the rest of the material. I have enjoyed this so far although I am not sure that all of the projects are related to what we will be asked to do in the real world. For example, The Excuse generator is very similar to the Domain Generator, and it was done twice, so it feels a bit repetitive sometimes. items.full_text: It was very overwhelming and very difficult if you don't have some good previous experience on coding, a very fast mind, or really a lot of time on your hands (not only 3 hours per day as said at the beginning of the course). The teaching material was not consistent (sometimes solutions to be found in the solutions.ipynb, sometimes not, sometimes instructions to be found on the 4geeks program platform, sometimes in the readme file, sometimes the theory of the lesson not being 100% useful for the lesson and module exercises, introducing difficult concepts from statistics and mathematics without explaining or even just giving a link where we could look the most important concepts up. Of course we should do our own research but so much as we had to do in this course is very difficult without becoming overwhelmed and working into the night if you have a full time job). Mentors were amazing but not available for the first month (or maybe even the first two?) of the course.

items.excerpt: Rushed! This, according to a number of my own community have asked how on Earth I was being expected to learn so much, so fast and on a part-time basis, going in fresh? Simply - I didn't. I took bits and pieces where I could and any questions I had...
items.full_text: Rushed! This, according to a number of my own community have asked how on Earth I was being expected to learn so much, so fast and on a part-time basis, going in fresh? Simply - I didn't. I took bits and pieces where I could and any questions I had in between could be left floating around for hours or days before I got a response which then overlapped with other modules - Doing 3 per week. I have spent the Monday, Wednesday & Friday as well as time alone as laid out by 4 Geeks but not knowing ´how to practice' let alone the help I could access in a timely fashion was inadequate. The syllabus was certainly interesting and the platform, for the most part was good at breaking down an abundance of information but the lack of guide to github, codespaces, to even not knowing I was 'saving them properly' were not met with proper instruction until someone 'finally' checked into my project submissions and a number of them being flagged as missing - adding to the frustration and disappointment.

items.excerpt: I believe this being a bootcamp it is supposed to be fast paced. Which isn't a problem but the quickness of registering the code on screen typing the code and actually understanding the code is hard to sustain at this speed. However, it does take as...
items.full_text: I believe this being a bootcamp it is supposed to be fast paced. Which isn't a problem but the quickness of registering the code on screen typing the code and actually understanding the code is hard to sustain at this speed. However, it does take as a developer time and experience to get the material. Videos are a good source for me if the time stamps where available as to what is being talked about it would be amazing. We are coming to the end of the session, and I don't believe we received enough raw material for students that wish to join the work force solo and not enter a job under more established names. Payment systems/ generating code and set up from scratch/ resources to go into the work force solo and tools for those students would be helpful as well.

We have done a couple of landing pages but then multiple generators for excuses, domain and even poker cards. I just would like the projects to be a more significant and creative. Also i think the dynamics of the class sometimes can be challenging. We have to focus on working on the project typically but I feel like I would work better on the projects on my own time and in class I would like it to be more interactive. like big part of getting a job is the interview and I feel like we could do more challenges in class where a student is asked to resolve a coding problem. I don't feel like this part is getting the importance it really has.

items.excerpt: I felt like the prework and Learnpacks that needed to be completed prior to the start of class were actually really helpful with getting me to learn beginner concepts. But I feel like once the class began, the instructor has been disorganized and...
items.full_text: I felt like the prework and Learnpacks that needed to be completed prior to the start of class were actually really helpful with getting me to learn beginner concepts. But I feel like once the class began, the instructor has been disorganized and unable to explain answers to exercises, comes to class unprepared with the exercises, and has been unresponsive/ hard to contact during breakout rooms. This most recent class (Monday) seemed to be better in terms of organization and communication after I had expressed to him my disappointment in his previous teaching style, although this time we were still not guided on how to do the exercises given even by the end of class.

items.excerpt: Xavier has been an *alright* mentor thus far. For the first few sessions, he seemed to be very unorganized and unprepared to be teaching (being unaware that we had completed the real estate cleanup project prior to the start of class and not having...
items.full_text: Xavier has been an *alright* mentor thus far. For the first few sessions, he seemed to be very unorganized and unprepared to be teaching (being unaware that we had completed the real estate cleanup project prior to the start of class and not having exercises ready for us to complete - and then gave us a messily-made copy-paste of some of the exercises). He has also seemed to struggle heavily with being able to give explanations to answers (only responding with "I'm not sure where that part comes from, it's just what the answer sheet says"). He is a kind person, but he spends too much of the class trying to be "funny" and does not seem to be able to explain the concepts/logic behind the code without having to just guess at what the A.I. code is generating. He seemed to be somewhat more ready this most recent class but we were still not guided properly on how to actually solve some of the exercises, only responding with "there are many right ways to do it".

items.excerpt: I am conflicted because I have seen how highly rated this course has been for others, and has even been recognized by many as one of the top coding bootcamps, but my experience in the classes so far has just been rough. I understand that some degree...
items.full_text: I am conflicted because I have seen how highly rated this course has been for others, and has even been recognized by many as one of the top coding bootcamps, but my experience in the classes so far has just been rough. I understand that some degree of it is my own lack of knowledge and that struggling is part of the learning process, but the learnpacks seemed to be more helpful than the instructor/course itself has been. I am only giving this a 3 because for the price, I would not recommend the bootcamp itself, but I would recommend just getting the learnpack/ learning modules off 4geeks.com

items.full_text: Overall, the bootcamp offers a solid introduction to full-stack development, but there is a notable issue with the Back-end component. The time allocated to teaching Back-end development is insufficient given its crucial role in being a well-rounded full-stack developer. This lack of depth in Back-end training means that students might not acquire the comprehensive skills needed to handle complex server-side logic and database management effectively. A more balanced approach, with additional focus on Back-end topics, would significantly enhance the program and better prepare participants for real-world development challenges.

items.excerpt: I think this programme is definitely not a beginners bootcamp. Pre-work videos of Alejandro Sanchez's weren't explanatory enough that's why I had to watch so many outside sources like youtube, edx, coursera videos from other creators. Also I think...
items.full_text: I think this programme is definitely not a beginners bootcamp. Pre-work videos of Alejandro Sanchez's weren't explanatory enough that's why I had to watch so many outside sources like youtube, edx, coursera videos from other creators. Also I think courses should be more practice based, not reading a powerpoint slide every course for 1.5 hours. That can be pre-recorded to be watched before classes so that we can profit more of the practice side. Lack of practice without supervision or a mentor made it super difficult for me to catch up and stay on track with the bootcamp so far. Also we only have two mentors which one is never available (Elisa) and the other is only available after evening hours which makes it difficult to catch up or do anything during the day.

items.full_text: The way that Laura Magallanes handled the issues that my cohort and I were having with such swiftness and efficiency, made me value 4Geeks Academy so much more. As our program manager I can tell she cares a lot about the overall experience that we have here, and that thoughtfulness has been so greatly appreciated. The depth of the information taught to us, as well as the range of projects as well, paired with our amazing instructor Samir, has made this experience so wonderful so far. I am truly grateful for the both of them. The only reason I am putting an 8 instead of a 10 is, based on my experience with the previous instructor, because I cannot confidently say that friends and family would get as amazing of an instructor as mine.

items.full_text:
How has your experience been studying Data Science and Machine Learning - 16 wks so far?

The curriculum needs a lot of work. From depth to organization to pacing. George has really come in clutch to help fill in the gaps- huge kudos to him. Biggest issue is organization or pedagogical approach. Different types of data need different approaches and bring a lot of baggage with each different approach. The current curriculum treats all data the same and focuses on modeling? Missed the target on that one. Also, the solutions that George has provided are vastly better on multiple levels. He has been crucial to any success in this.

items.full_text:
How has your experience been with your mentor George Perdrizet so far?

As mentioned in last comment, George has been completely crucial to any success in this course. He could still improve, and I will personally send some notes to him at some point, but he could structure more collaborative engagement and cohort-style relationship building (structured items during class as well as opportunities for engaging via slack outside of class). Cohort-based learning is powerful and we are missing a few of those items. However, he is clearly spending a lot of time making up for the shortcomings of the curriculum.

How was your experience in your mentoring with Valentina Ancieta?

I received an email from 4Geeks related to the workforce. It contained instruction to fill a questioner where you prive your resume, LinkedIn, GitHub, etc. and instructed to set up a 1-1 with your mentor in this case Valentina Ancieta. When I logged in she asked if I had finished the Career Support Course and then why haven’t I finished it or started it. This was not part of the initial email. At this point I felt she had not reviewed the information already provided and this was the intent of this meeting and made me feel I was wasting her time. So I decided to cut the meeting short. I would also like to change my career advisor at this time.

items.full_text: Sometimes it is hard to fully understand and follow the modules, but Alex and Carlos are both very knowledgeable, and I appreciate how they cater to everyone in the class. We are all on different levels when it comes to coding and software development, but they make it work for everyone. They are very patient, and I appreciate it very much. They cater to how each person learns. It is nice that the group is not too big so that they are able to do that. The nervousness I had before starting the program, is definitely gone. The atmosphere allows for me to feel comfortable no matter what level I am on compared to others who may be more advance. It is nice because I am learning from my instructors but also learning from classmates as well.

items.full_text:
How would you rate your teacher's performance today?

Rick's more concerned with the sound of his own voice than he is about actually ensuring that the students succeed. If we're learning algebra, Jandry or Matheus will ask something asinine like "Rick, is it true that math is used for rockets?" Rick will waste 25min talking about physics with the excuse of "not wanting to stifle their enthusiasm." Every. Single. Class. A responsible teacher will say "if you're interested, message me and I'll give you resources to read" or "we can discuss that later." These questions and Rick's responses create an irrelevant conversation where myself and others have to either wait or interrupt to ask any questions about what we are ACTUALLY supposed to be learning. We space out. If this class is a Rick+Jandry+Matheus special time then we should ALL get our money back. I 100% feel scammed. Maybe 3 people in this class could even hope to graduate unless everyone is rubber stamped. I'm not the bad guy. Rick is a clown and this cohort is a circus.

Ernesto is great!! He does a good job of holding standards of turning projects in on time while meeting us where we're at and reminds us if we feel like we're behind but we're genuinely putting in the time, other people feel the same way. I enjoy his humor as well, this 3 hour class would be horrific if we had a mentor with bad humor.

items.excerpt: I feel like I'm learning HOW to learn so even if it's fast paced and I like to take my time learning, I feel like I'm getting a really good lay of the land. I'm learning HOW to learn so anything else I need to learn or if there's holes in my...
items.full_text:
How has your experience been studying Full-Stack Software Developer 18w so far?

I feel like I'm learning HOW to learn so even if it's fast paced and I like to take my time learning, I feel like I'm getting a really good lay of the land. I'm learning HOW to learn so anything else I need to learn or if there's holes in my knowledge, I'm confident in my ability to fill in those knowledge gaps as I go. I've noticed I experience self doubt when I'm doing the practice problems because I have to look at the solutions often, but when I complete a project I understand big ideas and syntax confidently. I'm really enjoying the back to back JavaScript projects because I feel like I get my most learning out of doing the projects. I think I've learned more in the last 2 months than I would have on my own in 2 years and that's not an exaggeration.

items.full_text:
How has your experience been with your mentor George Perdrizet so far?

Extremely knowledgeable of the content and terrific at modeling and meeting students where they are. Despite mediocre curriculum, George is providing a lot of insights and supplemental materials. George could improve by establishing more cohort-based learning structures. For example, relationship-building and more impactful synchronous learning opportunities during classes. However, George is working with a cohort over varying abilities and doing a good job of meeting such a variety of needs.

items.excerpt: I love our professor (George). He is always ready and willing to help and is very knowledgable. He gets a 10/10. Its the course material that concerns me. Specifically the exercise solutions. I have caught multiple errors (both coding and dependency...
items.full_text: I love our professor (George). He is always ready and willing to help and is very knowledgable. He gets a 10/10. Its the course material that concerns me. Specifically the exercise solutions. I have caught multiple errors (both coding and dependency errors) in the solutions and confirmed they were errors by asking George about them. In some cases George has reviewed solutions provided by 4Geeks and informed us not to look at them due to the errors; he then provides his own solutions which are very helpful. In the beginning George was submitting pull request to fix the errors but no one on 4Geeks backend is approving his pull requests. I have paid thousands of dollars for this class and I think it is important that the exercise solutions are up to date, with clean code that is free of errors. It's normal to have a few errors here and there but at this point I don't even use the solutions to check my work and that is problematic.

items.full_text:
How has your experience been with your mentor Ernesto Medina so far?

My experience with Ernesto Medina has been fantastic. As our bootcamp teacher, he lightened dense lessons, popping up with a cake filter one moment, sporting a filter that placed sunny‑side‑up eggs over his eyes the next. He was very aware of whether we’d really understood a concept; if the first explanation didn’t land, he’d find a new approach, often drawing on personal experiences for extra context. Always beaming and ready to share his knowledge. He encouraged us to ask questions, cheered us on when the material felt overwhelming, and instilled the confidence that we truly can master full‑stack development. His patience, humor, and unwavering support made all the difference.

items.excerpt: The 4Geeks platform is intuitive, with comprehensive, hands‑on content, clear explanations, interactive exercises, and real‑world projects. I’d love a longer bootcamp to dive deeper into back‑end topics, while keeping the same depth for front‑end...
items.full_text:
How has your experience been with the platform and content so far?

The 4Geeks platform is intuitive, with comprehensive, hands‑on content, clear explanations, interactive exercises, and real‑world projects. I’d love a longer bootcamp to dive deeper into back‑end topics, while keeping the same depth for front‑end and the final project. Clean dashboard makes progress tracking seamless. Modules build logically from HTML/CSS to APIs and state management. Embedded editors and quizzes let you practice in place. Video walkthroughs, concise docs, and a responsive Slack community back you up. I would have liked to have more time on server‑side development (APIs, databases), this would be fantastic!

items.excerpt: Score might be higher if I wasn't the only computer nerd I know. I enjoy the confusion of learning to code and overcoming coding issues, whereas pretty much everybody I know would rather pull their hair out. That being said, it's a fun and...
items.full_text: Score might be higher if I wasn't the only computer nerd I know. I enjoy the confusion of learning to code and overcoming coding issues, whereas pretty much everybody I know would rather pull their hair out. That being said, it's a fun and well-organized program on the human side. There's a lot of very helpful people that seem to genuinely enjoy helping solve problems and focusing on getting you to understand what you're doing rather than just go through the motions. On the software side, I have noticed several issues regarding what seems to be mildly outdated lessons, and updates to the website causing issues for lesson layout and access. The LearnPack sometimes doesn't give enough information to understand what you're doing without guidance, and the objectives sometimes range from arbitrarily particular (where two things would work fine, only one is accepted) to far too loose (will say you're correct and let you move on without actually programming the intended effect correctly).

items.full_text:
How would you rate your teacher's performance today?

About 45 minutes of our meeting felt completely wasted. We were divided into groups to discuss our progress and the most challenging activities. In my group, no one spoke. Although I tried to moderate, it was mostly silent until the teaching assistant joined. He helped guide me through a particularly difficult activity, but by then it was almost 11 PM, so we couldn't accomplish much. After he left, time just dragged on. I was about to leave since the meeting had already exceeded three hours. Thankfully, I didn't, as the teacher ended the class shortly after. I strongly discourage these 'group activities' if they don't have a moderator present at all times.

items.full_text:
How would you rate your teacher's performance today?

While I truly appreciate the kindness and encouragement shown by both the lead teacher and his assistant, I must admit that I struggle with the use of breakout rooms. We've been divided into small groups twice now, each time for nearly an hour. Unfortunately, this time has felt largely unproductive. During the first session, no one in the group spoke until a classmate and I attempted to facilitate the conversation. Despite our best efforts, it wasn’t until the assistant teacher joined that the group became somewhat engaged.
