items.full_text:
How has your experience been studying Full-Stack Software Developer 18w so far?

Ernesto has been a fantastic teacher. Very attentive and nonjudgemental, and explains things very well. Really did a good job helping people feel comfortable learning a brand new skill. I feel like I've learned how to learn, and now I can learn anything code related I need to. I feel like I have the foundation I need to really propel myself. I'm very excited for the final project and I'm REALLY excited to have the time and skills to work on some projects I've been thinking of over the last 4 months as I've gone down this path. Thank you 4Geeks for making a fast paced and affordable coding bootcamp! I could not afford the other ones I was finding and they took a long time. I think this bootcamp was fast enough but also thorough enough to scan the field and understand the different pieces that make up the big picture of fullstack webdevelopment. My classmates and mentors and tutors, everyone is just really stellar. If I can work with people like this, I'll be so happy.

items.full_text:
How has your experience been studying Full-Stack Software Developer 18w so far?

I think this course is truly amazing: the structure, the instructors, the 4Geeks culture... It’s an exceptionally comprehensive program, covering every aspect needed to launch a career in development, from front end to back end (my favorite). I can’t believe it’s almost over—it flew by so quickly, and I’m a bit sad it’s ending, but this is just the beginning of my developer journey! Thanks to Ernesto and Slavina, especially Ernesto for being the ideal mentor to start this adventure. Thank you to all the mentors in my 1-on-1 sessions who kept me going, and to Laura, Daniel, and the admin team for their invaluable support throughout. It was daunting at first (and still is), but having such amazing people guide us made it so much smoother. Can’t wait to see what’s to come. Additionally, the daily live coding sessions, regular peer feedback, and hands-on projects reinforced each concept and created a collaborative, supportive atmosphere that boosted my confidence and practical skills. :-)

He also had 30 minute breakout rooms for a quick intro challenge to the lesson which was just the right length, not too long. He eased my doubts about how challenging the command line would be, and eased my anxiety about the class format with the right mix of whole-class versus individual participation.

items.full_text: While I think that the structure of our lessons are well thought-out, I find myself using the course as an outline rather than something I can follow along and practice. While I know it is designed for easy access and coding, from a personal standpoint I would like to learn industry standard practices such as cloning the repository locally. While the option was available in our projects, we are often pushed to use CodeSpaces which has had many technical issues. While I understand the goal is to do our own research for projects, the instructions are often vague and not many resources are provided for helping guide us through the project. Some resources are outdated as well. I think 4Geeks provides a great outline for Full-Stack development, however, I feel that it is missing some elements that make learning more effective.

How has your experience been with the platform and content so far?

The platform itself has been easy to use and access. It is easy to navigate the course on the 4Geeks webpage. While I think the content covers a lot of decent information, I also understand that much of the content was translated from another language making it difficult to follow sometimes. I find myself outlining the lesson and having to compare and find other resources to fill in gaps of understanding. Again, while I understand the goal is to facilitate a habit of research, having an unstable structure makes it difficult to know what to research for in a broader aspect.

items.full_text:
How has your experience been studying Full-Stack Software Developer FT - 9wks so far?

I think the course has great potential but there are a few concerns that I have had, and have spoken on that have not been addressed. 1. When working in code spaces there are far to many technical issues to make learning enjoyable. As someone who has been computer literate since childhood I have had far too many issues that made me feel as if continuing this course is even worth it. 2. The core instruction meaning the reading material was hard to connect with, and could have been presented better. For example there were times I did not understand the wording of a lesson because the grammar was unnecessarily wordy. 3. The pace of the instruction is at break neck speed, and as a visual learner I am finding it difficult to understand and absorb concepts I've only been given less than 24 hours to understand. 4. Although I am finally beginning to grasp some concepts I do not feel confident that I will be able to speak to the harder parts of the languages I've seen thus far.

items.full_text: I find myself seeking outside materials to understand what this course should be helping me to understand. I need the concepts in this course explained to me as if I am a five year old, and this course just doesn't do that for me. If the readings and exercises were presented in a way I could understand and feel comfortable grasping maybe then I would be more confident recommending this material to others. As an example I am finding myself seeking out the videos of the SuperSimpleDev on YouTube, and although I am starting from the beginning of his videos, I know that once I complete tasks from the examples his videos give me, I have a better understanding. This course I think is more suited to those who are not just beginning code, and is better suited to people who already have some type of foundational knowledge of the languages being presented, and just need the structure to learn better. The materials are also outdated, and learning a tutorial from a 7 year old video is nuts.

items.excerpt: Please refer to my previous comments about how I feel about the content, and platform, but just to reiterate. Code spaces is unnecessarily buggy, the course readings need to be plain and clear. Learn to explain the code to someone in their infancy...
items.full_text:
How has your experience been with the platform and content so far?

Please refer to my previous comments about how I feel about the content, and platform, but just to reiterate. Code spaces is unnecessarily buggy, the course readings need to be plain and clear. Learn to explain the code to someone in their infancy stage of learning code. I feel this would be the best way to succeed or continue forward in the Dallas market. Actually listen to the student when they are addressing their concerns about the technical issues. I also think that the pre-work should include learning how to navigate GitHub instead of waiting until further within the course, this could help alleviate frustration. 10 weeks is not enough time to learn extremely hard concepts if the person learning is not given a chance to absorb and practice the concepts before presenting the next concept.

The experience hasn't been as great as I thought it was. After being in the course for about 5 or 6 weeks I thought we would have more time to understand the course work and to be able to grasp the concepts of each programming language at least 2 or 3 days doing each project to get the understanding. It hard to learn when you have a new project due everyday, an you haven't understood the previous assignment I think we should had more time on each project at least 2 days no more than 3 days so we can get the full understanding of the projects to help flow along with the curriculum. I understand we signed up knowing this was like a full time job, but the original place was supposed to b Downtown so most of us had made the arrangements to go Downtown. When the location changed at the last minute it changed mostly everyone schedule most of us it take hour an 30 mins to get there it takes me 2 hours to get there and back home so it make it harder for me to study because I get home late.

items.full_text: I started the course without any prior knowledge. From the very first moment, I had the full support of the mentors, both in the classes and when it came to submitting projects. It has been an incredible experience, as they have made me passionate about ... the world of web programming, and I want to continue learning. items.full_text: For the past 16 weeks, I have been learning how to completely develop a web application at 4Geeks, and I have really enjoyed it. In the first weeks of the course, we covered the basics of front-end development (html, css, javascript, and react), as well ... as complementary technologies required for working in an office environment (git, command line, etc). Subsequently, the training focused on interacting with APIs, before creating one with SQLAlchemy, Python, and Flask. As well, we learned how to limit access to the API information. The last part of the course was a four-week final project that consisted of building a complete web application that put all the knowledge learned in the course to the test through a stream on the academy's YouTube channel. In each class, we had a teacher and an assistant who taught us the bases to carry out the exercises of the program meticulously. I have also benefited from unlimited mentoring provided by the school, which helped me to strengthen my knowledge and resolve any doubts I had throughout the bootcamp. In my opinion, the most valuable aspect of the academy is that all the teachers and mentors have been very willing to thoroughly teach me the content and to ensure that I understand the technologies. It's an atmosphere that's focused on total collaboration and helping you learn as much as possible (even remotely). 4Geeks is a great place to learn how to program, and with dedication on your part, you will surely learn a great deal about programming.

items.full_text: The pros are that you will have a large community supporting you. At the beginning you will be almost alone in the new world of programming when you do the pre-work for the course. However, once you get to know your teacher and the rest of the students ... you will gradually realize that this seemingly lonely environment is actually a community where we all face the same challenges. We all support each other gradually, of course at the beginning you will be somewhat reticent, reserved, because it is not normal to find yourself in a world where community support is the norm and being alone, reserved, isolated without helping others or being helped is the least usual, although you can opt for that path, but I warn you that it will not be easy to opt for that path. This is a path of challenges, defeats that soon become triumphs. At the beginning you feel helpless and incapable but as you advance, you overcome stagnations and generate those euphoric victories, you become addicted to this world of programming. Of course, all this is thanks to the immense support that you have from all sides along the bootcamp, you forget that you are in remote because as soon as you ask for help, (yes, you have to get used to confess something as difficult as "I can't, I'm stuck, I don't see the error" and they tell you, you are missing a semicolon in that line) all the mechanisms move in your favor to convert into victories those jams that seem to have no end. In conclusion, this bootcamp delivers like no other. It teaches you to be passionate about this world, but it also makes you wonder if this is really the path you want to follow. Because no matter how smart you are, this river only flows if you are really determined to move forward without fear of waterfalls. The teachers and mentors are wonderful, at least the one I had, Emanuel Martinez, taught me more than any of my teachers throughout my life. Victor and Marcos make things clear and always encourage you to keep going despite everyone. The treatment is personal, the platforms are ready to be used, and they help you at all times, even when they let you hit the ground with your face. After finishing the bootcamp they help you build a resume you would have never imagined, perfect your linkedin and know well what you need to do to get the attention of recruiters. And rest assured that if you don't know how to tackle a programming or job search problem you have lifetime mentoring, the 4Geeks Slack community that is IMMENSE and all the support of your mentors at your disposal. The best investment of my entire life. Thanks to this bootcamp my life finally has a way to go after being more than 5 years spinning from one job to another like a spinning top. Thank you, 4Geeks Academy

items.excerpt: I’ve been wanting to learn how to code but never found the time with a full time job, but then I saw 4GeeksAcademy offering a part time full stack bootcamp, and decided to spend a few hard months to learn. The part time structure was with 1 mentor...
items.full_text: I’ve been wanting to learn how to code but never found the time with a full time job, but then I saw 4GeeksAcademy offering a part time full stack bootcamp, and decided to spend a few hard months to learn. The part time structure was with 1 mentor and ... 1 assistant throughout the whole course for each lesson of 3 hours, 3 times a week, with a flip classroom concept of students are to learn before the class, and listen to explanation in class after already having gone through the material. The bootcamp has a good structure easing in the ‘coding mindset’ with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and eventually SQL and Python. If I were to give a negative feedback, it would be that the slowly easing in front end was making it rather easy to digest, but when it came to backend and endpoints, it was rather rushed comparing to the frontend part of the course - although I have to say I wasn’t an example student studying coding hardcore pushing everyday. For a full time working person, this is manageable, although I missed a few classes while traveling, Marta the mentor of my bootcamp offered mentorship sessions, to explain topics that I missed. I would definitely recommend - hours wise this is perfect for someone working full time office hours, although the 3x3 hours per week is not to be taken lightly - students are expected to learn and code on their own outside of the classes, to be able to follow the designed learning path. Mentors and assistants are very nice and friendly, passionate about coding as well as getting people to learn - the course also creates a great community within the class of ~6 people in my case, I believe it’s maximum 14 people in one class. There’s also lifetime support on the slack channels, finding a job, or just mentorship on anything. On the finance side, I have to say they offer a rather considerate support, they are in partnership with a payment/credit company, students can choose to pay in installments, as small as 100 euros a month, and obviously paying in full also works. (Not sure if this is only applicable in Europe)

items.full_text: After having researched 4Geeks, Wyncode, and IronHack, I settled on 4Geeks due to small class sizes, instructors' professional experience, and overall atmosphere. The smaller class atmosphere, I think, was far and away the largest advantage. I believe ... we had a 3-1 ratio of instructors to students which made for a fantastic learning environment considering the naturally frustrating challenges when learning to program. When I was learning on my own prior to the bootcamp, said challenges would often halt my progress and force me to take at least a few days of rest. With the support of mentors and experienced professionals immediately available (namely our teacher, Nacho), I was able to overcome such obstacles more quickly and with less energy spent on being upset. What's more, however, is I felt 4Geeks truly facilitated that "A-ha!" moment in programming to connect the dots. When you learn on your own, you often find yourself doing isolated exercises like learning how to write a for loop or an if-statement, etc., but don't really understand the point of those expressions outside of the immediate problem. 4Geeks, though, is absolutely phenomenal at piecing together concepts, expressions, and object-oriented programming for students. As a result, those formerly isolated exercises start to fit into the larger picture and once some clarity/understanding emerges you only become more interested, more invested, and more motivated to learn as much as possible and put your understanding to work in real-world applicable projects. I'm completely thrilled with the knowledge, experience, opportunities, and support 4Geeks continues to offer me and could not possibly have asked for more.

items.excerpt: What attracted me to 4Geeks Academy originally was the option of attending a part time cohort. For me, it meant I was able to continue my professional uninterrupted by a 3-4 month full-time course. I went in Mon & Wed 6-9 and Sat 9-12. Starting the...
items.full_text: What attracted me to 4Geeks Academy originally was the option of attending a part time cohort. For me, it meant I was able to continue my professional uninterrupted by a 3-4 month full-time course. I went in Mon & Wed 6-9 and Sat 9-12. Starting the cohort ... was a bit overwhelming for me as I had to get used to retraining myself how to approach a problem. The instructors at the academy do a pretty good job at trying to minimize the learning curve, but in reality they can only do so much with ~4 months of time to play with. Being a part-time course, a good portion of the learning falls on you and your motivation in your personal time. A lot of the assignments were the type where you learn *just* enough in class to go home and apply it yourself. Then, come back to the next class with any questions or concerns. There were absolutely times that were frustrating, and those frustrating moments hit everyone at different points. Luckily the team was very supportive/encouraging, and we managed to develop a kind of support group within the classmates. The course focused heavily on JavaScript/Reactjs for a large chunk of the time which, looking back, I appreciate because it’s the thing that I fell back on the most during the job interview that I got hired in. If you’re wondering whether they can teach you how to code - the answer is yes, but you have to put in a considerable amount of effort and time as well. They’ll lead you to the stream but you have to be the one to drink. 4Geeks has a well developed ecosystem of online resources as well as their knowledgeable staff that’ll do everything in their power to make sure you can surmount new topics and concepts. What’s was crazy for me was, because of imposture syndrome, (which you’ll likely have) I didn’t realize how much I had learned and was capable of until the very end when I had a functional final project that I was showing off to my peers. Above all, though, the most personally valuable skill I gained from the course was learning *how* to learn and teach myself. If I had been told that learning to learn would be one of my major take-always before signing up, I probably would have rolled my eyes. In reality, though, yes learning how to code is a big accomplishment (and with effort, you will), but in such a quickly evolving tech landscape where everything you need to know is available for free online, the most powerful tool you can have is your ability to pick up new skills and tricks to evolve with it. From what I saw, 4Geeks was working behind the scenes to make sure you gained that ability before they set you off into the world. 4Geeks hosts in-house meetups with local business from time-to-time to introduce their students to the industry. They’re a good opportunity make connections with local leaders as well as network with new and former 4Geeks students. I’ve heard of some students leveraging them to land interviews. I managed to get hired for my first tech job just a little before graduating (so I can’t personally speak on post-grad job support) which was great and very possible, but not exactly the norm. A few of my classmates also recently got hired within a few months after graduating (one of which I know what’s receiving job support from the academy). What’s amazing is after graduating I’d come back to 4Geeks whenever there was something that I couldn’t figure out at the new job and they (Alejandro and others) would *always be willing to set aside time for me and smooth out my confusions. All-in-all I would definitely recommend 4Geeks with the caveat that you only get out of it what you put in. However, if you’re motivated to change your life and can weather some inevitably stressful moments, you’ll do fine and be well positioned to transition into tech.

items.full_text: The pros are that you will have a large community supporting you. At the beginning you will be almost alone in the new world of programming when you do the pre-work for the course. However, once you get to know your teacher and the rest of the students you will gradually realize that this seemingly lonely environment is actually a community where we all face the same challenges. We all support each other gradually, of course at the beginning you will be somewhat reticent, reserved, becau... The pros are that you will have a large community supporting you. At the beginning you will be almost alone in the new world of programming when you do the pre-work for the course. However, once you get to know your teacher and the rest of the students you will gradually realize that this seemingly lonely environment is actually a community where we all face the same challenges. We all support each other gradually, of course at the beginning you will be somewhat reticent, reserved, because it is not normal to find yourself in a world where community support is the norm and being alone, reserved, isolated without helping others or being helped is the least usual, although you can opt for that path, but I warn you that it will not be easy to opt for that path. This is a path of challenges, defeats that soon become triumphs. At the beginning you feel helpless and incapable but as you advance, you overcome stagnations and generate those euphoric victories, you become addicted to this world of programming. Of course, all this is thanks to the immense support that you have from all sides along the bootcamp, you forget that you are in remote because as soon as you ask for help, (yes, you have to get used to confess something as difficult as "I can't, I'm stuck, I don't see the error" and they tell you, you are missing a semicolon in that line) all the mechanisms move in your favor to convert into victories those jams that seem to have no end. In conclusion, this bootcamp delivers like no other. It teaches you to be passionate about this world, but it also makes you wonder if this is really the path you want to follow. Because no matter how smart you are, this river only flows if you are really determined to move forward without fear of waterfalls. The teachers and mentors are wonderful, at least the one I had, Emanuel Martinez, taught me more than any of my teachers throughout my life. Victor and Marcos make things clear and always encourage you to keep going despite everyone. The treatment is personal, the platforms are ready to be used, and they help you at all times, even when they let you hit the ground with your face. After finishing the bootcamp they help you build a resume you would have never imagined, perfect your linkedin and know well what you need to do to get the attention of recruiters. And rest assured that if you don't know how to tackle a programming or job search problem you have lifetime mentoring, the 4Geeks Slack community that is IMMENSE and all the support of your mentors at your disposal. The best investment of my entire life. Thanks to this bootcamp my life finally has a way to go after being more than 5 years spinning from one job to another like a spinning top. Thank you, 4Geeks Academy

items.full_text: I’ve been wanting to learn how to code but never found the time with a full time job, but then I saw 4GeeksAcademy offering a part time full stack bootcamp, and decided to spend a few hard months to learn. The part time structure was with 1 mentor and 1 assistant throughout the whole course for each lesson of 3 hours, 3 times a week, with a flip classroom concept of students are to learn before the class, and listen to explanation in class after already having gone through the ma... I’ve been wanting to learn how to code but never found the time with a full time job, but then I saw 4GeeksAcademy offering a part time full stack bootcamp, and decided to spend a few hard months to learn. The part time structure was with 1 mentor and 1 assistant throughout the whole course for each lesson of 3 hours, 3 times a week, with a flip classroom concept of students are to learn before the class, and listen to explanation in class after already having gone through the material. The bootcamp has a good structure easing in the ‘coding mindset’ with HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and eventually SQL and Python. If I were to give a negative feedback, it would be that the slowly easing in front end was making it rather easy to digest, but when it came to backend and endpoints, it was rather fast paced comparing to the frontend part of the course - although I have to say I wasn’t an example student studying coding hardcore pushing everyday. For a full time working person, this is manageable, although I missed a few classes while traveling, Marta the mentor of my bootcamp offered mentorship sessions, to explain topics that I missed. I would definitely recommend - hours wise this is perfect for someone working full time office hours, although the 3x3 hours per week is not to be taken lightly - students are expected to learn and code on their own outside of the classes, to be able to follow the designed learning path. Mentors and assistants are very nice and friendly, passionate about coding as well as getting people to learn - the course also creates a great community within the class of ~6 people in my case, I believe it’s maximum 14 people in one class. There’s also lifetime support on the slack channels, finding a job, or just mentorship on anything. On the finance side, I have to say they offer a rather considerate support, they are in partnership with a payment/credit company, students can choose to pay in installments, as small as 100 euros a month, and obviously paying in full also works. (Not sure if this is only applicable in Europe)

items.full_text: I started the course in April and currently I am in the final phase, working with my team on the final project. It has been a roller coaster of emotions and feelings, but I would definitely do it again. Throughout the course we got support from both our teacher and the teacher assistant. You can ask for mentorship sessions to build up on certain things or, in case you did not understand something, to review. It is very important that you ask questions. Revise, read everything there i... I started the course in April and currently I am in the final phase, working with my team on the final project. It has been a roller coaster of emotions and feelings, but I would definitely do it again. Throughout the course we got support from both our teacher and the teacher assistant. You can ask for mentorship sessions to build up on certain things or, in case you did not understand something, to review. It is very important that you ask questions. Revise, read everything there is to read and attend those sessions. You can't just attend the classes and call it a day. You need to program outside of the scheduled classes as well and the more you do, the better for you. Every module has at least one project, which has several levels and you can add more functionalities. I always tried to personalize things to make them more interesting. Sky really is the limit! At the beginning things look very overwhelming and scary, but once you notice the pattern and you reflect upon your progress, you realize that it works. You just need to have faith in the course and the way things are done. Talk to your classmates, to your teachers. Don't believe what that little voice in your head is telling you. Everybody struggles, some people are doing the exercises faster, some people are slower. Some are better in one module, but completely suck at the other one. Just keep on coding, it will get easier after some time. What I do definitely recommend is to reduce working hours when working on the final project. If you can, even take a vacation. Don't underestimate the task, you will need to code every single day and you most probably will face some technical issues which will require time.

An excellent alternative for starting out in the world of programming For the past 16 weeks, I have been learning how to completely develop a web application at 4Geeks, and I have really enjoyed it. In the first weeks of the course, we covered the basics of front-end development (html, css, javascript, and react), as well as complementary technologies required for working in an office environment (git, command line, etc). Subsequently, the training focused on interacting with APIs, before creating one with SQLAlchemy, Python, and Flask. As well, we learned how to limit access to the API information. The last part of the course was a four-week final project that consisted of building a complete web application that put all the knowledge learned in the course to the test through a stream on the academy's YouTube channel. In each class, we had a teacher and an assistant who taught us the bases to carry out the exercises of the program meticulously. I have also benefited from unlimited mentoring provided by the school, which helped me to strengthen my knowledge and resolve any doubts I had throughout the bootcamp. In my opinion, the most valuable aspect of the academy is that all the teachers and mentors have been very willing to thoroughly teach me the content and to ensure that I understand the technologies. It's an atmosphere that's focused on total collaboration and helping you learn as much as possible (even remotely). 4Geeks is a great place to learn how to program, and with dedication on your part, you will surely learn a great deal about programming.

items.full_text: 4Geeks Academy presents a very well-designed FullStack bootcamp, in my opinion. It provides a fair amount of knowledge in several technologies that are heavily demanded in the market nowadays. It equips you with the proper tools to navigate the course with ease, allowing you to focus on what is important: learning. BUT, this is not a miraculous solution; it all depends on your dedication and time. You still need to learn A LOT on your own if you want to succeed quickly (I've been working on my programming skills almost like a full-time job since I started the bootcamp, and it took me 6 months after finishing it to land a job). Don't get me wrong: this is the same for every bootcamp. It's impossible to reach a professional level in programming in just 3 months by only attending classes. That being said, if you think you have the time and the strength, 4Geeks is just an amazing academy. Not only do they teach you the skills, but they also teach you how to keep learning. Also, I probably wouldn't have had this job opportunity if it weren't for the amazing career support they provide after the course. Now I know how to navigate this world, and that's just as valuable as the skills themselves. I absolutely recommend you to check what they have to offer!

items.full_text: I started the course in April and currently I am in the final phase, working with my team on the final project. It has been a roller coaster of emotions and feelings, but I would definitely do it again. Throughout the course we got support from both our teacher and the teacher assistant. You can ask for mentorship sessions to build up on certain things or, in case you did not understand something, to review. It is very important that you ask questions. Revise, read everything there is to read and attend those sessions. You can't just attend the classes and call it a day. You need to program outside of the scheduled classes as well and the more you do, the better for you. Every module has at least one project, which has several levels and you can add more functionalities. I always tried to personalize things to make them more interesting. Sky really is the limit! At the beginning things look very overwhelming and scary, but once you notice the pattern and you reflect upon your progress, you realize that it works. You just need to have faith in the course and the way things are done. Talk to your classmates, to your teachers. Don't believe what that little voice in your head is telling you. Everybody struggles, some people are doing the exercises faster, some people are slower. Some are better in one module, but completely suck at the other one. Just keep on coding, it will get easier after some time. What I do definitely recommend is to reduce working hours when working on the final project. If you can, even take a vacation. Don't underestimate the task, you will need to code every single day and you most probably will face some technical issues which will require time.

items.full_text: I really recommend this course to anyone who wants to get started in the world of programming, especially to those who have 0 previous knowledge in the subject. The selection of technologies, the very good teachers that the program has and the organization of the topics in terms of complexity and learning curve, are very well balanced. Being a student of the Full-Time mode, I can say that it requires absolute willingness and exclusive dedication during the entire training time, there is no other way, it is necessary to make the sacrifice, but the result is unobjectionable, one really acquires the basic skills necessary to develop at the end of the course a complete basic Full-Stack project, which indicates a first big step towards the goal of becoming a professional developer. Overall, 4Geeks delivers what it promises, giving you the initial basic tools to become a Full-Stack programmer, but here is a caveat, once you finish the training program, you have to continue studying, learning new technologies and making projects, but this will happen in any other bootcamp or even once you graduate from an IT university career. What big technologies you will learn? Backend: Basic Flask/Python, FrontEnd: Basic React with Hooks(No useReducer, no Redux)/Bootstrap 5, FullStack Deployment with Render

items.excerpt: For the past 16 weeks, I have been learning how to completely develop a web application at 4Geeks, and I have really enjoyed it. In the first weeks of the course, we covered the basics of front-end development (html, css, javascript, and react), as...
items.full_text: For the past 16 weeks, I have been learning how to completely develop a web application at 4Geeks, and I have really enjoyed it. In the first weeks of the course, we covered the basics of front-end development (html, css, javascript, and react), as well as complementary technologies required for working in an office environment (git, command line, etc). Subsequently, the training focused on interacting with APIs, before creating one with SQLAlchemy, Python, and Flask. As well, we learned how to limit access to the API information. The last part of the course was a four-week final project that consisted of building a complete web application that put all the knowledge learned in the course to the test through a stream on the academy's YouTube channel. In each class, we had a teacher and an assistant who taught us the bases to carry out the exercises of the program meticulously. I have also benefited from unlimited mentoring provided by the school, which helped me to strengthen my knowledge and resolve any doubts I had throughout the bootcamp. In my opinion, the most valuable aspect of the academy is that all the teachers and mentors have been very willing to thoroughly teach me the content and to ensure that I understand the technologies. It's an atmosphere that's focused on total collaboration and helping you learn as much as possible (even remotely). 4Geeks is a great place to learn how to program, and with dedication on your part, you will surely learn a great deal about programming.

items.full_text: Joining 4geeks has been a life changing experience. from the first time i reached out to them until now on the cusp of graduation the 4geeks team has gone above and beyond what i expected from them. My situation was very complicated as i lived on the other side of the world and had a 12 hour difference from the other students and teachers. Despite that setback the instructors and staff ahve always been available and friendly. The teachers are excellent and have a wealth of knowledge. apart from the curriculum my instructor sprinkled in his own nuggets of information when he had time. One of my favorite aspects of the course was the mentoring program (which is available even after graduation). Here there is a staff of teachers who are available to have 1- 1 meetings about pretty much anything you can think of related to programming/coding. The core curriculum is extensive and gives a solid background in several languages. looking back at where i was at the beginning of the course to now... the difference is night and day and i feel so much more confident when approaching new material now. There are also mini talks and presentations related to applying to jobs and different aspects of coding. Choosing to join 4geeks is one of the best decisions i have made in my life!

items.full_text: Before you officially start the program, they give you pre-work that consists mainly HTML & CSS. I had exposure to HTML and CSS before starting the boot camp which did help me a little. So if you want to learn a little about HTML and CSS before starting the program it’s always helpful but not a necessity. You’re going to learn a LOT. Don’t feel discouraged if you don’t feel ready enough in one area when the program progresses to another concept. The 4Geeks community is really helpful and kind, they’ll help you with anything. They have mentors you can schedule sessions with to help you with assignments or questions that you have. Everyone there wants you to succeed. Once you’re a part of the 4Geeks family, you’re there forever. With any bootcamp or learning resource, it’s really about the time and energy you put into something. There are tons of exercises and projects that they have for you, as well as class instruction where you work on projects in class. Don't be shy to ask for help! They really do encourage you to schedule mentoring sessions and may even have "study group" sessions once a week with a TA to help with the current assignments you're working on. Take advantage of the resources available! Unrelated to the boot camp, one advice I keep seeing and hearing is when you learn enough to build a simple project, build, build, build! You’ll have plenty to build within the program, but in general always keep building and using Google for what you know. I always think I understand something until I start building lol so applying your knowledge is key!

items.full_text: This bootcamp had all the technologies that are most valued in the industry right now. Even though there are a few more you may still need to fit some jobs. However, its good because we get pushed to figure out how to look up information on our own, to find answers or solidify concepts. In other words, I am glad I took a loan for this (this bootcamp is one of the most affordable one I found), because I was struggling to teach myself coding and feeling overwhelmed, with no one to really rely on for guidance or feedback. I also can see other students getting jobs and posting about jobs in our slack channels, overall this is a solid investment for those willing to put the work in.

items.full_text: My experience has been very good with 4Geeks. For me, the part that I thought was the best is the teachers concern for their students and willingness to help them, and the fact that they let you take the course again, no questions asked, if you feel you need to. That is exactly what I did, since the first time I went through the bootcamp I was working a lot and didn't feel like I was able to give it my all. Like any school or human, there were good parts and bad, but overall I think for the price and what you get, they did an excellent job. Some schools charge nearly double and end up teaching the same or less than 4Geeks, so for those reasons I would encourage people to attend.

items.full_text: My experience with 4geeks was and continues to be very rewarding. If you are interested in coding, you should consider this bootcamp. The community-like approach is what convinced me. It has been refreshing to learn in an environment that encourages collaboration and innovation. The leadership is super friendly and helpful. Plus they have knowledgeable mentors that will patiently help you out. The course itself is robust and complete. It moves fast, but it’s doable. You will learn enough about front and back-end to get going. You will be surprised of how much you know once you complete the final project. If you are seriously interested in coding… don’t think about it too much and do it.

items.full_text: I came across 4Geeks after doing some research on the internet (as one does). There are multiple aspects that differentiated them from other bootcamps. Their curriculum is truly what first got my attention! It was full-stack and involved python. Next, was the price of the Bootcamp. It was important to me that I found a good curriculum that was worth the value that they offered. After meeting with one of the founders, I realized they were the fit for me and immediately applied. They had the best value for the syllabus that I was looking for. From the beginning, they offered an endless amount of support for any type of question that I had. This was important to me because I am enrolled in the part-time cohort and was not able to see them every day. Their communication is incomparable to other courses I have tried. Outstanding to say the least. Since I have started, I have not been disappointed. I have learned so much in the past 12 weeks (of 16) and am so proud of my progress. I graduate in September and am looking forward to the job support they have promised me. I am confident that they will help me succeed even after I have graduated and moved into my career.

items.full_text: I graduated from the part-time full stack program at 4Geeks academy and I had a great experience. I had no coding background and felt that it moved at a fast enough pace to Be able to complete a full project by then end but slow enough that with dedicated time and discipline I was able to keep up. I really like that you have access to a teacher or mentor pretty much 24/7 via slack or office hours to ask questions. After graduating you continue to have that same support which is great. I was able to get tutoring well after I graduated to continue to sharpen my skills and practice.
